frozenCoreMeaning.zh-Hans: 这张牌代表多个驱动力权重接近时可能形成的资源与注意分散。
frozenCoreMeaning.en: A potential dispersion of resources and attention when several drivers carry similar weight.

zh-Hans.title: 分散
zh-Hans.subtitle: 注意与资源被多个相近优先级切开

sections.title: 一句话理解
paragraphs: 当太多事情同时需要关注，真正的问题可能不是目标不正确，而是每个方向都获得了一部分资源，却没有任何一项得到足够集中的投入。有效的安排，是选择当前阶段最值得完成的事项，让其他方向暂时保留，而不必同时执行。

sections.title: 这张卡想提醒什么？
paragraphs: 生活中，我们可能同时拥有许多合理的计划。工作需要改善流程，事业希望发展新产品，个人想学习新的能力，家庭也有各种安排等待处理。每一件事单独来看都值得投入，因此很容易产生一种想法：既然都重要，就应该同时开始。
然而，开始一项工作与完成一项工作，需要的条件并不相同。当注意力不断在不同任务之间切换，我们可能需要反复回想之前做到哪里、重新整理资料，或者再次进入原本的思考状态。即使每天都很忙，真正完成的成果却可能没有明显增加。
「分散」邀请你观察：目前是否有太多方向同时保持活动，而没有明确哪一项应该优先完成？
有些计划并不需要被取消，只是不适合在当前阶段同时执行。暂缓一项有价值的事情，不等于否定它的意义。相反，给予一项重要工作足够的时间和资源，可能更容易让它真正完成，随后再为其他方向创造空间。
集中不是永远只做一件事，而是在适当阶段，避免让所有事情都争夺相同的注意力。

sections.title: 现实中可能如何出现？
paragraphs: 工作、产品与多项目管理
假设一个团队同时开发电子书功能、自动化报告、新的顾客页面以及其他服务。每个项目都有合理的发展价值，但它们都需要同一批人员进行设计、测试和验证。
当所有项目都被标记为优先事项，团队可能每天在不同工作之间切换。许多功能已经完成大部分，却迟迟没有经过完整验收。
「分散」提醒团队，可以根据已有承诺、实际风险与可用资源，确定一个阶段性主要交付目标。其他项目则保留清楚记录与后续安排，不必同时持续开发。
这样做不是减少长期目标，而是让真正重要的成果有机会进入可使用的状态。
家庭与个人安排
一个家庭可能同时计划装修、整理财务资料、安排孩子活动及购买新的家庭用品。
如果每项计划都立即展开，时间和预算便可能不断被切分，原本重要的生活安排也容易受到影响。
更有效的方式，可能是先完成最影响日常生活的一项工作，再根据家庭成员的需要与实际条件安排其他计划。
不是所有想做的事情，都必须在同一个星期或月份完成。
学习与职业发展
一个人可能同时报名数据分析、项目管理、软件开发和沟通技巧课程，希望尽快增加自己的能力。
但如果学习时间有限，每门课程都只能进行一点，便可能缺乏足够的练习来形成实际成果。
「分散」提醒你，可以先选择一项与当前目标最相关的技能，完成一个小型实践项目，再决定是否进入其他领域。
这样，学习不仅持续增加知识，也能够逐渐形成可检验的能力证据。

sections.title: 什么做法更有帮助？
paragraphs: 保留多个可能，但只让适当数量的事情进入当前执行阶段。
可以先将所有计划区分为：
- 当前必须进行： 涉及重要责任、明确期限或现阶段关键成果。
- 下一阶段再进行： 有价值，但目前不需要主动投入。
- 需要重新评估： 已不符合实际需要，或长期没有明确用途的事项。
在此基础上，选择一个能够被清楚验收的阶段性成果，并为它安排相对稳定的执行时间。
集中并不意味着忽略紧急事务。必要的顾客服务、安全问题、家庭照顾及其他正式义务仍然需要及时处理。

sections.title: 什么情况需要留意？
paragraphs: 分散最需要留意的风险，是将「每个项目都有进展」误认为整体正在有效前进。
如果大量工作始终停留在未完成状态，参与者可能花费越来越多时间追踪任务、恢复上下文和协调不同项目，而不是完成实际成果。
另一种风险，是认为集中意味着必须永久放弃其他兴趣和目标。事实上，阶段性优先只是当前的资源安排，可以根据真实情况重新检查。
同时，也不应为了追求集中，而让整个团队只依赖一个关键项目，忽略已经存在的必要责任或风险。
有效集中需要合理的完成标准，也需要允许其他方向在适当时间重新进入执行。

sections.title: 现在可以做什么？
paragraphs: 选择目前同时进行的几项工作或计划，完成一次简单的「阶段性集中检查」。
1. 列出事项： 目前有哪些项目同时占用注意力？
2. 确认优先： 哪一项最值得在当前阶段真正完成？
3. 暂缓其他： 选择一至两项可以合理暂停的非紧急工作。
4. 明确完成标准： 什么实际结果出现，才代表主要事项完成？
5. 重新安排： 完成后再检查其他项目何时适合恢复。
这次练习不是让你放弃其他可能，而是减少不断切换所产生的消耗。

zh-Hans.frozenObservationQuestion: 现在有哪些事情可以暂时不动，让一件真正重要的事完成？
interpretationBoundary: 固定卡义用于观察和反思，不证明你目前的经历、能力或张力，也不预测未来。
这张卡描述的是 ECR 模型中多个相近优先级可能造成的注意力与资源分散，并不表示系统已经确认你缺乏专注能力、存在注意力障碍或无法有效管理工作。实际问题仍需要根据任务数量、执行条件、资源安排及可观察的结果判断。
sourceProposedQuestion: 现在有哪些事情可以暂时不动，让一件真正重要的事完成？

en.title: DISPERSION
en.subtitle: Attention and resources are split across similar priorities

sections.title: At a Glance
paragraphs: When too many activities demand attention, the issue may not be that the goals are wrong. Resources may simply be spread too thinly for any one objective to progress meaningfully. A workable approach is to select a priority for the current stage while keeping other possibilities open without actively pursuing all of them.

sections.title: What This Card Invites You to Consider
paragraphs: We may have several reasonable plans at once. Work processes need improvement, a business has new products to develop, personal skills deserve attention, and household matters also require action. Each objective may be worthwhile individually, making it tempting to begin everything simultaneously.

Starting an activity, however, is different from completing it. Constantly switching between tasks can require us to recover earlier context, reorganize information, and rebuild concentration. We may remain busy every day without producing a corresponding number of completed outcomes.
Dispersion invites you to examine whether too many directions remain active without a clear priority for completion.

Some projects do not need to be abandoned; they may simply be unsuitable for simultaneous execution. Postponing something worthwhile does not make it unimportant. Concentrating enough resources on one meaningful outcome may allow it to be completed, creating more room for other directions afterward.
Concentration does not mean doing only one thing forever. It means preventing every objective from competing for the same attention at the same time.

sections.title: How It May Appear in Real Life
paragraphs: Work, Products & Multiple Projects

Imagine a team developing an ebook feature, automated reports, new customer pages, and additional services at the same time. Each project has potential value, yet all depend on the same people for design, testing, and verification.
When everything is treated as a priority, the team continually shifts between workstreams. Numerous features may become nearly complete without passing end-to-end acceptance.

Dispersion suggests choosing a primary delivery objective based on existing commitments, practical risks, and available resources. Other projects can remain documented and scheduled without staying in active development.
This does not reduce long-term ambitions. It gives important outcomes a realistic opportunity to become usable.
Family & Personal Responsibilities
A household may be planning renovations, organizing financial records, arranging children's activities, and purchasing household items.
If every plan begins at once, time and budgets may become fragmented, potentially disrupting essential routines.
A more workable approach may be to complete the task that most affects everyday life before scheduling other plans according to the household's needs and available resources.
Not everything worth doing needs to happen in the same week or month.
Learning & Career Development
Someone may enroll in data analysis, project management, software development, and communication courses in the hope of expanding their capabilities quickly.
With limited study time, however, each subject may receive too little practice to produce meaningful outcomes.
Dispersion suggests choosing a skill closely related to the current objective and completing a small practical project before expanding into other areas.
Learning can then produce observable evidence of capability rather than only an increasing collection of course materials.

sections.title: A Helpful Approach
paragraphs: Keep several possibilities available, but allow only a manageable number into active execution.
Organize commitments into:
- Must proceed now: Essential obligations, firm deadlines, or critical current outcomes.
- Suitable for a later stage: Valuable initiatives that do not require immediate execution.
- Needs reassessment: Activities that no longer fit actual needs or lack a clear purpose.
Then select an outcome with defined completion criteria and allocate sufficiently consistent time to it.
Concentration does not mean ignoring urgent responsibilities. Essential customer service, safety concerns, caregiving, and other valid obligations still require appropriate attention.

sections.title: What to Watch For
paragraphs: The principal risk of Dispersion is confusing progress across many projects with meaningful overall advancement.
When substantial work remains unfinished, increasing amounts of time may be spent tracking tasks, recovering context, and coordinating workstreams rather than completing useful outcomes.

Another risk is believing concentration requires permanently abandoning other interests or goals. A temporary priority is simply a resource decision for the current stage and can be reviewed as circumstances change.
Concentration should also not mean depending entirely on a single project while overlooking essential obligations or important risks.
Effective concentration needs clear completion criteria and a reasonable way for other priorities to re-enter execution later.

sections.title: One Small Action
paragraphs: Choose several activities currently competing for your attention and try a simple concentration review.
1. List the activities: Which projects remain active?
2. Identify the priority: Which outcome most deserves completion during the current stage?
3. Pause appropriately: Select one or two nonurgent activities that can reasonably wait.
4. Define completion: What observable result would establish that the main task is finished?
5. Reschedule: Review when other projects should resume after the priority has been completed.
The purpose is not to abandon other possibilities, but to reduce the costs of constant switching.

en.frozenObservationQuestion: What could remain still for now so one important thing can finish?
interpretationBoundary: Fixed card meanings invite observation and reflection. They do not establish your current experiences, abilities or tensions, or predict the future.

This card describes potential dispersion of attention and resources among similarly weighted priorities within the ECR model. It does not establish that you lack concentration, have an attention-related condition, or are unable to manage work effectively. Actual difficulties should be assessed through tasks, operating conditions, resource allocation, and observable outcomes.
sourceProposedQuestion: What could remain still for now so one important thing can finish?

audit.question: EXACT_FROZEN_MATCH
terminologyAndBoundaries: 类似权重驱动力的分散风险，不是注意力诊断。
audit.personalFactConclusion: No live customer facts exported; no semantic approval inferred.

frozenCoreMeaning.zh-Hans: 这张牌代表限制、承载或边界让多个需求集中在有限容量中的张力。
frozenCoreMeaning.en: Tension created when constraints, holding, or boundaries concentrate many demands into limited capacity.

zh-Hans.title: 压缩
zh-Hans.subtitle: 太多内容被要求留在有限空间内

sections.title: 一句话理解
paragraphs: 当有限的时间、资源或空间已经容纳太多要求，继续增加内容可能让整体安排更加困难。真正有帮助的，不一定是扩大容量，而是重新辨认什么必须保留、什么可以退出，让重要的事情重新获得运行空间。

sections.title: 这张卡想提醒什么？
paragraphs: 生活中，许多压力并不是突然出现，而是随着新的要求不断加入，逐渐形成的。一项工作流程最初只有几个必要步骤，后来增加更多检查、表格与审批；一个家庭的时间表不断加入课程、活动和其他安排；个人的每月收入则需要同时支付越来越多固定支出。
这些内容单独来看，可能都有存在的理由。然而，当每一项都被认定为不可删减，有限的容量便会逐渐变得拥挤。
「压缩」邀请你观察：目前是否有太多内容被要求同时保留，却没有足够空间让它们正常运作？
有时候，我们会尝试通过更紧密的安排来解决问题。例如缩短每项工作的时间、减少活动之间的间隔，或者进一步压缩预算。但如果原本的安排已经缺少必要的弹性，这些做法可能增加错误、冲突与额外成本。
真正值得思考的是：哪些条件确实不能改变？哪些只是因为过去一直存在，所以从来没有被重新评估？
有价值的压缩管理，不是把所有东西塞进更小的空间，而是为真正重要的部分保留足够空间。

sections.title: 现实中可能如何出现？
paragraphs: 工作与流程管理
假设一个部门原本只需要填写一份生产记录。随着业务发展，管理者陆续增加品质检查、成本记录、进度报告和不同形式的审批。
这些要求可能各有用途，但如果没有检查重复内容，员工便可能花费越来越多时间填写表格，实际生产和问题处理的时间反而减少。
「压缩」提醒管理者，可以先确认哪些记录涉及必要的质量、财务或合规责任，哪些属于重复输入，哪些资料能够在适当控制下合理复用。
重点不是取消重要检查，而是减少没有实际价值的重复，让工作流程重新获得执行空间。
家庭、时间与生活空间
一个家庭可能同时安排孩子的学校、课外活动、家庭聚会、日常家务及其他成员的工作时间。
如果所有活动都被视为必须参加，日程便可能没有足够的休息、交通和临时调整空间。
适当的改善，不一定是把每项活动安排得更加紧密，而是重新确认哪些活动目前最重要，哪些可以减少频率或暂缓。
家居空间也存在类似情况。当有限的房间或储物区域不断加入新家具和用品，继续增加收纳工具未必能够改善使用体验。先辨认真正需要保留的物品，可能比继续挤入更多东西更有效。
财务与固定责任
假设一个家庭每月收入大致稳定，但贷款、保险、教育及其他持续支出逐渐占据大部分现金流。
即使所有付款目前仍然能够完成，能够用于突发需要或未来安排的资金空间可能已经十分有限。
「压缩」提醒你，先区分必须履行的合同责任、基本生活支出，以及具有调整弹性的安排。
某些固定支出可能需要通过合理预算重新分配；某些服务可以依据真实需要检查是否继续使用；涉及贷款、保险或法律义务的事项，则必须核对正式条件，不能直接停止支付。
真正的目标是改善可用资金空间，而不是为了让预算看起来更宽松，就忽略仍然存在的责任。

sections.title: 什么做法更有帮助？
paragraphs: 先减少不必要的拥挤，再决定是否需要增加容量。
面对有限空间中的过多要求，可以先区分三个类别：
- 必须保留： 涉及基本需要、安全、合规、重要承诺与必要运行的部分。
- 可以调整： 能够减少频率、简化方式或重新安排的部分。
- 可以退出： 已经失去实际用途、重复存在，或目前不再需要的部分。
不要只根据某件事情存在多久来决定是否保留，也不要只因为它看起来不重要，就忽略其可能涉及的正式义务。
当非必要内容合理减少，原本的安排可能无需进一步扩大，就已经能够恢复一定的灵活性。

sections.title: 什么情况需要留意？
paragraphs: 压缩最需要留意的风险，是把所有内容都定义为不可失去。
当每项任务、物品、费用或规则都被视为必须保留，任何新的需要都只能被继续挤入现有安排。久而久之，系统可能越来越缺乏调整能力。
另一种风险，是为了释放空间而过度删减。某些内容虽然平时不常使用，却在安全、应急、合规或长期保障方面具有重要作用。删除之前，仍然需要确认其真实功能。
有效的压缩管理，既不坚持保留一切，也不为了减少数量而牺牲必要保障。

sections.title: 现在可以做什么？
paragraphs: 选择一个目前显得特别拥挤的领域，例如工作流程、家庭时间表、储物空间或每月预算。
1. 列出内容： 哪些事情正在占用有限空间或资源？
2. 确认必要性： 哪些必须保留？为什么？
3. 寻找可退出部分： 哪些属于重复、过时或当前不再需要？
4. 释放一点空间： 合理减少、合并或移除一项非必要内容。
5. 观察结果： 是否更容易处理真正重要的事情？是否保留了必要保障？
不需要一次清除所有内容。先恢复一点能够实际使用的空间。

zh-Hans.frozenObservationQuestion: 什么其实可以退出，换取更大的运行空间？
interpretationBoundary: 固定卡义用于观察和反思，不证明你目前的经历、能力或张力，也不预测未来。
这张卡描述的是 ECR 模型中有限容量与过多保留要求之间可能出现的张力，并不代表系统已经确认你处于严重压力、财务困难或其他现实问题。释放空间不意味着可以忽略法定义务、必要照顾、安全要求或有效合同。实际删减与调整必须依据相关事实和责任判断。
sourceProposedQuestion: 什么其实可以退出，换取更大的运行空间？

en.title: COMPRESSION
en.subtitle: Too much is being held inside limited space

sections.title: At a Glance
paragraphs: When limited time, resources, or space must accommodate too many demands, adding more can make the entire arrangement harder to manage. The useful response is not always to expand capacity, but to distinguish what must remain from what can be removed, creating room for what matters.

sections.title: What This Card Invites You to Consider
paragraphs: Many pressures develop gradually as additional requirements accumulate. A workflow may begin with a few essential steps and later gain more checks, forms, and approvals. A household schedule may continually acquire new lessons and activities. An individual's monthly income may need to support an increasing number of fixed expenses.
Each demand may appear reasonable on its own. But when everything is considered non-negotiable, limited capacity becomes increasingly crowded.
Compression invites you to examine whether too many requirements are being retained without enough room for them to function properly.

A common response is to make arrangements even tighter: shorten each task, reduce the gaps between commitments, or compress the budget further. Yet when an arrangement already lacks flexibility, these measures can increase errors, conflicts, and additional costs.
The useful question is which conditions genuinely cannot change and which have simply remained unquestioned because they have existed for a long time.
Managing compression is not about fitting everything into less space. It is about preserving enough room for what genuinely matters.

sections.title: How It May Appear in Real Life
paragraphs: Work & Process Management
Imagine a department that originally required one production record. As operations expand, management adds quality checks, cost records, progress reports, and several forms of approval.
Each requirement may serve a purpose, but without reviewing duplication, employees may spend increasing amounts of time completing forms while having less time for production and problem-solving.
Compression suggests identifying which records are necessary for quality, financial control, or compliance, which involve duplicate entry, and which information can be appropriately reused.
The objective is not to remove essential controls. It is to reduce unnecessary duplication and restore workable capacity.
Family, Time & Living Space
A household may coordinate school, extracurricular activities, family gatherings, domestic tasks, and changing work schedules.
If every activity is treated as essential, the calendar may leave insufficient room for rest, travel, or unexpected changes.
The solution may not be tighter scheduling, but reconsidering which activities currently matter most and which can become less frequent or wait.

Physical space can present a similar problem. When more furniture and belongings enter a limited room or storage area, adding further organizers may not make the space more usable. Identifying what genuinely needs to remain may be more effective than fitting in more items.
Finances & Fixed Commitments
Imagine a household with broadly stable monthly income, while loans, insurance, education, and other continuing expenses occupy an increasing share of cash flow.
Even if current payments remain manageable, little flexibility may be left for unexpected needs or future plans.
Compression suggests distinguishing contractual obligations and essential living expenses from arrangements with greater flexibility.

Some expenses may be reorganized through budgeting, while optional services can be reviewed against actual needs. Loans, insurance, and legal obligations require attention to their formal terms and cannot simply be discontinued.
The goal is to improve available financial room without concealing responsibilities that still exist.

sections.title: A Helpful Approach
paragraphs: Reduce unnecessary crowding before deciding whether more capacity is needed.
When limited space contains too many demands, distinguish:
- Must remain: Essential needs, safety, compliance, important commitments, and critical operations.
- Can be adjusted: Activities whose frequency, method, or timing can change.
- Can be removed: Duplicated, obsolete, or currently unnecessary elements.
Do not retain something merely because it has existed for a long time, or remove it without checking whether it supports a valid obligation.
When unnecessary requirements are reduced, an arrangement may regain flexibility without requiring substantial additional capacity.

sections.title: What to Watch For
paragraphs: The principal risk of Compression is treating every element as something that cannot be lost.

When every task, item, expense, or rule becomes non-negotiable, new requirements can only be forced into the existing arrangement. Over time, the system may lose the flexibility needed to respond to change.

Another risk is removing too much in pursuit of space. Some elements are rarely used but remain important for safety, emergencies, compliance, or long-term protection. Their actual purpose should be examined before removal.
Effective management of compression neither preserves everything nor sacrifices essential safeguards simply to reduce the number of commitments.

sections.title: One Small Action
paragraphs: Choose an area that feels especially crowded, such as a workflow, household schedule, storage space, or monthly budget.
1. List what occupies it: Which elements use the limited space or resources?
2. Confirm what is essential: What must remain, and why?
3. Identify what could leave: Which elements are duplicated, outdated, or no longer necessary?
4. Create some room: Appropriately reduce, combine, or remove one nonessential element.
5. Review the result: Is it easier to manage what matters? Have essential safeguards been preserved?
You do not need to remove everything at once. Begin by restoring a little genuinely usable space.

en.frozenObservationQuestion: What could leave in exchange for more operating space?
interpretationBoundary: Fixed card meanings invite observation and reflection. They do not establish your current experiences, abilities or tensions, or predict the future.

This card describes potential tension between limited capacity and excessive retained demands within the ECR model. It does not establish that you are experiencing severe stress, financial difficulty, or another specific problem. Creating space does not justify disregarding legal obligations, essential care, safety requirements, or valid contracts. Practical reductions must be guided by actual circumstances and responsibilities.
sourceProposedQuestion: What could leave in exchange for more operating space?

audit.question: EXACT_FROZEN_MATCH
terminologyAndBoundaries: 约束内过多需求；不能借精简取消有效义务。
audit.personalFactConclusion: No live customer facts exported; no semantic approval inferred.

frozenCoreMeaning.zh-Hans: 这张牌代表反馈、持续性或未关闭问题可能形成重复运行。
frozenCoreMeaning.en: Feedback, continuity, or unresolved structures may form a repeating runtime.

zh-Hans.title: 反复
zh-Hans.subtitle: 反馈持续回来，却没有形成真正更新

sections.title: 一句话理解
paragraphs: 有些问题之所以不断出现，不一定是因为我们没有努力解决，而可能是每一次处理都只改善了眼前的情况，却没有改变问题再次发生的条件。真正有帮助的，是让重复出现的反馈，成为改变理解、条件或回应方式的依据。

sections.title: 这张卡想提醒什么？
paragraphs: 生活中，有些事情似乎总在重复。一个工作问题已经处理过几次，却仍然不断发生；家庭成员反复讨论相同的安排，过了一段时间又回到原来的状况；个人制定了新的计划，却在相似条件下再次遇到相同困难。
这些情况不一定说明过去没有付出努力。有时候，每一次处理确实暂时解决了问题，只是原本造成问题的条件没有改变。
「反复」邀请你观察：当相同的反馈再次出现时，这一次是否带来了新的理解？还是我们只是重新执行上一次的处理方式？
例如，某个文件每次出错都由工作人员手动修复。文件虽然能够继续使用，但如果产生错误的流程没有改善，工作人员就可能需要长期重复相同工作。
真正值得注意的，不只是问题再次出现，而是每次处理之后，有没有留下可以减少未来重复的改变。
当然，重复不一定是负面的。定期检查、持续练习和必要维护，本来就需要反复进行。反复 关注的是那些持续产生相同困难，却没有形成有效更新的重复过程。

sections.title: 现实中可能如何出现？
paragraphs: 工作、系统与重复故障
假设一家公司的订单资料经常出现不一致。每次发生时，员工都会重新核对数据，修正错误，然后继续处理。
这些修正能够解决当次问题，但下个月仍然出现类似情况。
「反复」提醒团队，可以进一步检查错误是否来自相同的资料输入方式、字段定义、交接流程或验证条件。
如果已经确认存在共同原因，可以针对该环节改善流程，而不是仅仅增加处理错误的人手。
但也不能因为问题外观相似，就直接认定每次原因相同。真正的改善仍然需要记录与验证。
家庭、关系与重复沟通
家庭成员可能反复因为相同的时间安排发生争论。每一次讨论后，大家暂时达成共识，但下一次工作时间改变，又出现相似的问题。
这不一定代表某个人故意不配合，而可能是沟通之后仍然没有明确谁负责通知变化、什么时候需要确认，以及出现冲突时采用什么备用安排。
有效的回应，不只是要求大家以后更加注意，而是尝试建立适合所有参与者的实际协调方式。
如果问题涉及他人的意愿或关系中的界限，也需要通过适当沟通确认，而不是单靠自己的推测解释重复发生的原因。
财务、预算与持续缺口
假设一个家庭连续几个月发现实际结余低于原本预算，每次都通过临时减少某项支出来应对，但类似情况仍然出现。
这时，可能值得检查的不是某一次消费，而是预算是否遗漏了固定责任、非每月发生的费用，或收入与付款时间之间的差异。
如果实际记录支持这些原因，可以重新调整预算结构和资金预留方式，再观察后续结果。
但财务缺口可能由不同因素造成，不能因为它反复出现，就直接认定某一种原因。涉及贷款、投资或重大财务责任时，仍需要结合真实资料与适当专业意见判断。

sections.title: 什么做法更有帮助？
paragraphs: 不要只检查问题有没有再次出现，也要检查上一次处理究竟改变了什么。
面对反复出现的困难，可以先确认三个方面：
- 重复的是什么？ 是相同结果、相同条件，还是只是外观看起来相似？
- 上次怎样处理？ 当时解决了什么？哪些条件没有改变？
- 这次可以改变什么？ 是需要补充资料、调整流程、明确责任，还是建立新的检查方式？
不一定需要重新设计整个系统。有时候，一个经过验证的具体调整，就能够减少长期重复的工作。

sections.title: 什么情况需要留意？
paragraphs: 反复最大的风险，是让相同的问题逐渐变成被习惯接受的背景状况。
当某项错误或困难已经出现很多次，参与者可能不再认为它值得重新检查，而只是按照过去的方式处理。虽然每次都付出了时间，却没有减少未来继续处理的需要。
另一种风险，是把所有重复都理解成必须改变。有些活动本来就具有周期性，也可能已经拥有适当的处理流程。并非每一次重复都代表原有结构存在问题。
真正需要改变的，是那些持续产生不必要成本、而现有处理方式又没有改善其发生条件的循环。

sections.title: 现在可以做什么？
paragraphs: 选择一个最近已经出现至少两次、而且仍然需要重复处理的问题。
1. 记录重复： 它分别在什么情况下发生？
2. 比较原因： 两次情况有什么共同点，又有什么不同？
3. 检查旧回应： 上一次处理解决了什么？留下了什么？
4. 改变一个条件： 尝试调整一项有证据支持的流程、责任或回应方式。
5. 验证结果： 经过适当时间，再检查问题是否减少，或者出现了什么新的反馈。
不要只是把同样的事情再做一次。尝试让这一次的经验，真正改变下一次的条件。

zh-Hans.frozenObservationQuestion: 这个问题再次出现时，什么必须和上一次做得不一样？
interpretationBoundary: 固定卡义用于观察和反思，不证明你目前的经历、能力或张力，也不预测未来。
这张卡描述的是 ECR 模型中反馈或未解决事项可能形成的重复运行，并不表示系统已经确认你存在固定行为模式、心理问题或不断失败的经历。重复事件是否具有共同原因，仍需根据实际记录和适当验证判断。
sourceProposedQuestion: 这个问题再次出现时，什么必须和上一次做得不一样？

en.title: LOOP
en.subtitle: Feedback returns repeatedly without producing real update

sections.title: At a Glance
paragraphs: Some problems keep returning not because no effort has been made, but because each response addresses the immediate situation without changing what allows it to recur. Meaningful progress uses recurring feedback to improve understanding, conditions, or the way the problem is addressed.

sections.title: What This Card Invites You to Consider
paragraphs: Recognizable patterns can recur in everyday life. A workplace problem may be addressed several times but continue returning. Family members may repeatedly discuss an arrangement only to encounter the same difficulty again. A personal plan may be restarted, yet similar obstacles continue appearing under familiar circumstances.
This does not necessarily mean earlier efforts were ineffective. Each response may have solved the immediate problem while leaving the conditions that produce it unchanged.
Loop invites you to ask whether recurring feedback is leading to a different understanding or whether the same response is simply being repeated.

For example, an employee may repair an incorrect file whenever the error appears. The file becomes usable again, but if the process producing the error remains unchanged, the same manual repair may be required indefinitely.
The important issue is not merely that a problem returns. It is whether each response contributes to reducing future recurrence.

Repetition itself is not necessarily harmful. Regular checks, sustained practice, and essential maintenance naturally involve repeated actions. LOOP concerns recurring difficulties that continue without meaningful changes to understanding or operating conditions.

sections.title: How It May Appear in Real Life
paragraphs: Work, Systems & Recurring Problems
Imagine a company experiencing recurring inconsistencies in order records. Each time, employees reconcile the data, correct the errors, and continue working.
The immediate problem is resolved, but a similar situation appears the following month.
Loop suggests examining whether the errors share a common cause, such as data entry methods, field definitions, handovers, or verification conditions.
If a recurring cause is established, improving that part of the process may be more useful than continually increasing the effort spent correcting errors.
Similar-looking problems do not automatically have identical causes, however. Reliable improvement still requires records and verification.
Family, Relationships & Repeated Conversations
Family members may repeatedly disagree over scheduling. After each discussion, an agreement is reached, but similar difficulties return when work arrangements change again.

This does not necessarily mean someone is deliberately uncooperative. The discussion may never have established who communicates changes, when confirmation is needed, or what backup arrangement applies.
A useful response may involve agreeing on a practical coordination process rather than simply asking everyone to be more careful next time.
Where personal preferences or boundaries are involved, clarification should come through appropriate communication rather than assumptions about other people's motives.
Finances, Budgets & Recurring Gaps
Imagine a household repeatedly finding that its available balance is lower than budgeted. Each month, it responds by temporarily reducing an expense, yet the same difficulty returns.
It may be worth examining whether the budget overlooks recurring obligations, nonmonthly expenses, or differences between when income arrives and payments are due.
If actual records support these explanations, the household can revise its budgeting or cash-allocation arrangements and evaluate subsequent results.

Financial gaps can have different causes, however. Recurrence alone does not prove a particular explanation. Decisions involving debt, investment, or significant obligations require actual records and appropriate professional judgment.

sections.title: A Helpful Approach
paragraphs: Do not examine only whether the problem has returned. Examine what actually changed after the previous response.
For a recurring difficulty, consider:
- What is repeating? Is it the same result, the same conditions, or merely a similar appearance?
- How was it handled previously? What was resolved, and what remained unchanged?
- What could change this time? Is better information, a revised process, clearer responsibility, or a different verification method needed?
A complete redesign is not always necessary. Sometimes one verified adjustment can reduce substantial recurring work.

sections.title: What to Watch For
paragraphs: The main risk of Loop is allowing a recurring difficulty to become accepted background noise.

When an error or obstacle has appeared many times, those involved may stop investigating and simply follow the usual response. Time is spent repeatedly without reducing the need for future intervention.

Another risk is assuming that all repetition requires change. Some activities are naturally recurring and may already have appropriate procedures. Repetition alone does not establish a structural problem.
The patterns worth addressing are those that continue creating unnecessary costs while the existing response fails to improve the conditions producing them.

sections.title: One Small Action
paragraphs: Choose a difficulty that has occurred at least twice and continues requiring repeated attention.
1. Record the recurrence: Under what circumstances did it appear?
2. Compare the causes: What was similar, and what was different?
3. Review the previous response: What did it resolve, and what remained?
4. Change one condition: Test an evidence-supported adjustment to the process, responsibility, or response.
5. Verify the result: After an appropriate period, check whether the difficulty has decreased and what new feedback emerged.
Rather than simply repeating the previous solution, use this experience to improve the conditions for what happens next.

en.frozenObservationQuestion: When this issue returns, what must be different from last time?
interpretationBoundary: Fixed card meanings invite observation and reflection. They do not establish your current experiences, abilities or tensions, or predict the future.

This card describes the possibility of recurring feedback or unresolved processes within the ECR model. It does not establish that you have a fixed behavioral pattern, a psychological condition, or a history of repeated failure. Whether recurring events share a cause must be determined through actual evidence and appropriate verification.
sourceProposedQuestion: When this issue returns, what must be different from last time?

audit.question: EXACT_FROZEN_MATCH
terminologyAndBoundaries: 重复反馈的可能性；不能断定用户有固定心理模式。
audit.personalFactConclusion: No live customer facts exported; no semantic approval inferred.

frozenCoreMeaning.zh-Hans: 这张牌代表系统为了避免进一步负荷、冲突或不确定性，开始减少输入、连接与开放程度。适度收紧有时是必要的保护，但当这个过程持续扩大，原本用于维持稳定的边界可能逐渐变成限制，使新的资源、关系、讯息或变化难以进入。
frozenCoreMeaning.en: This card describes a system reducing input, connection, and openness to avoid further load, conflict, or uncertainty. Some contraction can be protective, but if it keeps expanding, boundaries that once preserved stability can become restrictions that block new resources, relationships, information, or change.

zh-Hans.title: 封闭
zh-Hans.subtitle: 为了保护稳定，系统逐渐减少新的输入与连接

sections.title: 一句话理解
paragraphs: 当外部要求太多时，暂时减少输入与联系，可以帮助我们保护重要的生活和工作安排。但如果保护不断扩大，连有益的资讯、支持与机会也无法进入，原本的边界便可能从保护变成限制。

sections.title: 这张卡想提醒什么？
paragraphs: 生活中，我们有时需要主动减少外部干扰。一个团队为了完成重要项目，可能暂时停止接受新的功能要求；一个家庭在特别忙碌的时期，可能减少非必要活动；一个人在经历持续的冲突后，也可能需要保留私人空间，让自己能够重新安排生活。
这些选择不一定是逃避。适当的收紧，可以帮助有限的时间和资源重新集中，也能保护隐私、安全及必要的稳定。
「封闭」邀请你进一步观察：这些保护措施是否仍然符合最初的需要？
例如，团队原本只想在产品交付前暂停新功能开发，但后来逐渐停止收集所有顾客反馈；家庭为了减少压力而暂缓活动，却慢慢失去获得外部协助的机会；一个人为了避免无效沟通而减少联系，却连原本可靠的支持也不再接触。
当这种情况出现，问题不一定是边界太多，而可能是原本有范围的保护，逐渐变成没有明确检查条件的持续封闭。
真正有效的保护，需要同时知道什么应该暂时挡在外面，以及什么仍然应该保留进入的渠道。
封闭不意味着必须立即重新开放一切。有些关系、资讯或外部要求确实不安全、不适合，或已经超出合理的个人界限。是否重新开放，应以实际需要、信任、同意和安全条件为依据。

sections.title: 现实中可能如何出现？
paragraphs: 工作、系统与顾客反馈
假设一个团队正在准备重要系统上线。为了减少开发风险，管理层决定暂时冻结新增功能，只处理必要的错误和交付问题。
这个决定可能十分合理。但如果团队后来把所有顾客意见都视为干扰，连已付款用户报告无法下载的问题也不再接收，那么保护范围就可能超过原本的目的。
「封闭」提醒团队，可以继续暂停非紧急功能，同时保留处理安全问题、实际故障及必要顾客反馈的渠道。
保护开发稳定，不等于关闭真实世界的反馈。
家庭、关系与个人空间
一个家庭可能因为工作与照顾责任增加，决定暂时减少聚会和其他活动，以保留休息与照顾孩子的时间。
这样的边界可以很有帮助。但如果之后出现可靠的照顾支持或适合家庭的活动，也不必因为过去一直选择减少接触，就自动排除所有可能。
在个人关系中也是如此。减少令人不适或不安全的接触可能是合理的，甚至是必要的；但是否与其他可信任的人保持联系，应当由个人根据实际需要与安全状况决定。
重新开放不是义务，而是在合适条件下保留选择的能力。
财务、资讯与外部机会
假设一个人曾经因为复杂的投资资讯或不可靠的推销而感到困扰，于是决定不再关注任何相关信息。
避免误导性的推销、诈骗及高风险承诺，确实是重要的保护措施。但如果连银行正式通知、合同变更或必要的保障资料也完全忽略，就可能错过需要及时处理的责任。
更合适的安排，可能是停止接触未经核实的宣传，同时保留查看正规账户通知、合同文件和适当专业意见的渠道。
保护自己的财务安全，并不要求接受所有资讯，也不应该完全失去了解重要变化的途径。

sections.title: 什么做法更有帮助？
paragraphs: 明确保护的目的、范围，以及什么时候值得重新检查。
面对一项正在持续收紧的安排，可以先问：
- 保护什么？ 是安全、隐私、休息、关键工作，还是有限的资源？
- 限制什么？ 哪些输入、联系或活动确实造成不必要的负担？
- 保留什么？ 哪些重要资讯、责任与可靠支持仍应有适当的进入渠道？
可以考虑采用有范围的保护。例如暂停新项目，但保留必要故障报告；减少非必要社交，但不妨碍获取可信的协助。
如果现实条件改变，再判断是否适合调整原有边界。不需要为了证明自己开放而勉强接受不必要或不安全的接触。

sections.title: 什么情况需要留意？
paragraphs: 封闭 最需要留意的风险，是将过去有效的保护措施无限扩大。
当外部环境已经变化，原来的限制却从未重新检查，系统可能越来越依赖少量已有资讯与资源。即使出现可靠的新建议、必要的协助或更好的方法，也可能因为习惯拒绝新的输入，而难以进入。
另一种风险，则是因为担心自己过于封闭，就过早取消仍然必要的边界。
有些保护涉及真实的隐私、安全、法律责任或个人选择，不能仅为了增加交流而被撤除。某个人希望保留私人空间，也不等于他必须向别人解释或证明这种选择。
真正值得避免的，不是保护本身，而是没有重新评估条件，就让保护变成永久限制。

sections.title: 现在可以做什么？
paragraphs: 选择一项你为了减少干扰、风险或压力而建立的限制。
1. 确认目的： 当初为什么需要这项保护？
2. 检查现状： 原本的风险或负荷现在是否仍然存在？
3. 辨认价值： 哪些限制仍然有效？哪些可能挡住了有益的资讯或支持？
4. 调整一个边界： 在安全、适当且自愿的条件下，保留一条必要的反馈或支持渠道。
5. 观察结果： 重要部分是否仍然得到保护？新安排是否带来真正有用的帮助？
如果原本的风险仍然存在，维持边界也可以是合理的结果。目标不是增加所有输入，而是确认保护仍然符合现实需要。

zh-Hans.frozenObservationQuestion: 目前有哪些保护动作仍然有必要，哪些已经从保护变成了限制新的输入？
interpretationBoundary: 固定卡义用于观察和反思，不证明你目前的经历、能力或张力，也不预测未来。
这张卡描述的是 ECR 模型中为了维持稳定而减少输入与连接的潜在张力，并不代表系统已经确认你存在社交退缩、心理障碍或不合理的防御行为。适当的隐私、安全及个人边界应当受到尊重。是否重新开放某项联系，需要依据真实条件、个人意愿与必要的安全保障决定。
sourceProposedQuestion: 目前有哪些保护动作仍然有必要，哪些已经从保护变成了限制新的输入？

en.title: WITHDRAWAL
en.subtitle: The system narrows new input and connection to protect stability

sections.title: At a Glance
paragraphs: When external demands become excessive, temporarily reducing input and contact can help protect important arrangements. But when those restrictions keep expanding and block useful information, support, or opportunities, boundaries that once provided protection may become limitations.

sections.title: What This Card Invites You to Consider
paragraphs: Sometimes reducing external input is necessary. A team may temporarily stop accepting new feature requests to complete an important release. A household may reduce optional activities during a demanding period. Someone who has experienced repeated conflict may need personal space to restore a manageable routine.
These choices do not necessarily represent avoidance. Appropriate contraction can help preserve limited resources, protect privacy, and maintain essential stability.
Withdrawal invites you to examine whether protective measures still serve their original purpose.

A team may initially pause new development but gradually stop listening to all customer feedback. A household may reduce activities to manage demands but unintentionally lose access to useful outside support. Someone may limit unproductive communication and eventually become disconnected from people who previously offered reliable assistance.
The concern is not necessarily that boundaries exist, but that protection originally intended to be limited has become an ongoing restriction without a clear basis for review.
Effective protection recognizes what should remain outside and which channels for useful information or support should remain available.

Withdrawal does not mean everything must be reopened immediately. Some relationships, information sources, or external demands may genuinely be unsafe or unsuitable. Reopening should depend on actual needs, trust, consent, and safety—not pressure to become more available.

sections.title: How It May Appear in Real Life
paragraphs: Work, Systems & Customer Feedback
Imagine a team preparing for an important software release. To reduce development risk, management temporarily freezes new features and concentrates on essential defects and delivery requirements.

This may be entirely reasonable. But if the team eventually treats all customer messages as interruptions, including reports that paying users cannot access their purchases, the restriction may have expanded beyond its purpose.
Withdrawal suggests keeping nonurgent development on hold while preserving channels for security concerns, actual failures, and essential customer feedback.
Protecting development stability does not mean closing the system to real-world evidence.
Family, Relationships & Personal Space
A household may reduce gatherings and optional activities during a period of increased work and caregiving demands, protecting time for rest and essential routines.

That boundary can be useful. If reliable caregiving support or suitable activities later become available, the family can evaluate them rather than automatically rejecting everything because withdrawal was previously necessary.

The same distinction matters in personal relationships. Reducing distressing or unsafe contact may be appropriate or essential. Whether to maintain contact with other trusted people should remain a personal decision based on needs and safety.
Reopening is not an obligation. It is about preserving the ability to choose when conditions are appropriate.
Finances, Information & Opportunities
Imagine someone becoming overwhelmed by complex investment information or unreliable financial promotions and deciding to stop following financial information altogether.

Avoiding misleading promotions, scams, and inappropriate commitments is an important safeguard. Yet ignoring official account notices, contractual changes, or essential coverage information could result in missed obligations.
A more workable arrangement may be to avoid unverified promotions while maintaining access to legitimate account communications, contractual documents, and appropriate professional guidance.
Protecting financial security does not require accepting every source of information, nor should it eliminate access to important developments.

sections.title: A Helpful Approach
paragraphs: Clarify what the protection is for, what it restricts, and when it deserves review.
For an arrangement that has become increasingly restrictive, ask:
- What is being protected? Safety, privacy, rest, essential work, or limited resources?
- What is being restricted? Which inputs, contacts, or activities create unnecessary demands?
- What should remain accessible? Which important information, responsibilities, and reliable sources of support still need appropriate channels?
Consider bounded protection. New projects may be paused while essential incident reports remain available. Optional social contact may be reduced without preventing access to trusted assistance.
When circumstances change, reassess whether the boundary still fits. There is no need to accept unnecessary or unsafe contact simply to demonstrate openness.

sections.title: What to Watch For
paragraphs: The central risk of Withdrawal is allowing a previously useful protective measure to expand without review.

When external conditions change but restrictions remain unchanged, an arrangement may become increasingly dependent on a narrow set of familiar information and resources. Reliable suggestions, necessary assistance, or better approaches may remain inaccessible because new input is routinely rejected.
The opposite risk is removing necessary boundaries too quickly out of concern about being overly withdrawn.

Some protections concern genuine privacy, safety, legal obligations, or personal choices. They should not be removed merely to increase communication. Someone's decision to maintain personal space does not automatically require justification to others.
The concern is not protection itself, but allowing it to become permanent restriction without examining whether the conditions still justify it.

sections.title: One Small Action
paragraphs: Choose a restriction you introduced to reduce interference, risk, or pressure.
1. Clarify its purpose: Why was this protection originally needed?
2. Review current conditions: Does the original risk or burden still exist?
3. Examine its effects: Which restrictions remain useful, and which may block valuable input or support?
4. Adjust one boundary: Where safe, appropriate, and voluntary, preserve one necessary channel for feedback or assistance.
5. Observe the outcome: Is what matters still protected? Does the change provide genuinely useful support?
If the original risk remains, maintaining the boundary may be the appropriate outcome. The goal is not to increase all input, but to ensure protection still matches reality.

en.frozenObservationQuestion: Which protective moves are still necessary, and which have begun to restrict useful new input?
interpretationBoundary: Fixed card meanings invite observation and reflection. They do not establish your current experiences, abilities or tensions, or predict the future.

This card describes a potential tension within the ECR model involving reduced input and connection in pursuit of stability. It does not establish social withdrawal, a psychological condition, or inappropriate defensiveness. Reasonable privacy, safety, and personal boundaries deserve respect. Decisions about reopening contact should reflect actual conditions, individual choice, and necessary safeguards.
sourceProposedQuestion: Which protective moves are still necessary, and which have begun to restrict useful new input?

frozenCoreMeaning.zh-Hans: 这张牌代表能量、场域支持或可用容量下降时的持续成本。
frozenCoreMeaning.en: The continuing cost that can arise as energy, field support, or available capacity declines.

zh-Hans.title: 耗散
zh-Hans.subtitle: 运行失去能量或支持，却仍持续占用容量

sections.title: 一句话理解
paragraphs: 当一件事情获得的资源、支持或实际回报逐渐减少，继续维持过去的投入强度，未必能够恢复原有成果。真正有帮助的，是辨认哪些部分仍值得维持，哪些需要降低强度、恢复资源或适当结束。

sections.title: 这张卡想提醒什么？
paragraphs: 生活中的许多安排，都需要持续投入才能维持。一项事业需要时间、资金和人员支持；家庭生活需要成员之间的协调与照顾；一个长期项目也需要足够的关注和维护资源。
这些条件不会永远保持相同。某项服务可能逐渐减少顾客需求，一项工作可能失去原本的团队支持，或者生活进入新的阶段后，过去能够投入的时间已经不再充足。
「耗散」邀请你观察：目前有没有某项事情，已经无法获得过去相同的支持，却仍然占用相同甚至更多资源？
有时候，我们因为已经投入大量努力，便希望继续维持原来的规模和强度。成果减少了，就投入更多时间；资源不足了，就尝试额外承担；一项计划已经不再适合，却因为不愿放弃过去的成果而持续维护。
这种做法可能暂时延长运行，但不一定能够改善实际情况。
真正值得思考的，不只是如何维持原有安排，还包括它是否仍然值得以过去的强度继续运行。
适当降低投入，不一定代表失败。有些项目可以转入维护阶段，有些责任可以重新分配，也有些活动已经完成主要价值，适合妥善结束。
耗散提醒我们：当支持条件已经改变，运行强度也可能需要随之改变。

sections.title: 现实中可能如何出现？
paragraphs: 工作、产品与运营成本
假设一家公司曾经推出一项受欢迎的数字产品。经过一段时间，顾客需求逐渐减少，但团队仍然按照最初的规模持续更新、宣传和维护。
如果实际收入与使用率不断下降，维护这项产品可能开始占用本来可以支持其他重要服务的资源。
「耗散」提醒团队先检查实际数据：需求是否真的持续下降？产品是否仍然承担重要顾客权益或合约责任？继续维护需要多少资源？
如果必要责任已经得到保障，部分功能可能适合降低维护频率、整合到其他服务，或按照适用条件逐步结束。
重点不是一发现需求下降就立即停止服务，而是让持续投入与真实价值保持合理关系。
家庭与持续照顾
一个家庭可能长期按照固定方式分配家务与照顾责任，但随着工作时间和家庭需要改变，原本能够提供协助的人减少了。
如果依旧要求同一个成员维持过去的全部安排，就可能使日常协调越来越困难。
「耗散」邀请家庭重新检查现有支持：哪些照顾责任仍然必须履行？哪些活动可以降低频率？哪些任务需要重新分工或引入可靠协助？
减少非必要活动，可以为重要照顾保留资源。但不能因为支持减少，就忽略孩子、长者或其他需要照顾者的基本需要。
真正合适的调整，应当让必要责任继续受到保障，同时改善长期维持安排的可行性。
财务、资产与持续支出
假设某项资产过去能够提供稳定收入，但近期收入减少，同时维修、贷款或管理费用仍然存在。
如果继续按照过去的收益预期投入同样资源，实际现金流可能承受越来越大的压力。
「耗散」提醒你，根据真实收入、必要支出与合同责任重新评估安排，而不是因为过去表现良好，就默认未来仍然值得维持相同投入。
可能的选择包括改善管理、调整非必要费用、重新评估长期计划，或在充分了解财务与法律后果后考虑其他安排。
这张卡不能决定是否出售资产或停止投资。它只是提醒：过去的价值，不应代替对当前条件的判断。

sections.title: 什么做法更有帮助？
paragraphs: 让持续投入与当前真正可用的资源及价值保持一致。
可以先检查三个方面：
- 支持是否改变？ 时间、资金、人员、实际需求或其他资源是否已经下降？
- 什么仍然重要？ 哪些责任、成果或保障必须继续？
- 强度是否适合？ 哪些活动可以降低频率、减少范围、重新分配或妥善结束？
如果一项工作仍然具有必要价值，可以考虑建立更低成本、可持续的维护方式。
如果某项活动已经达到原本目标，或者不再值得维持相同投入，则可以评估适当的交接与结束条件。

sections.title: 什么情况需要留意？
paragraphs: 耗散最大的风险，是把资源或支持下降理解为必须立即投入更多的讯号。
某个项目表现不如过去，便持续增加宣传与开发；一项安排已经难以维持，却不断要求同一批人员投入更多时间。
这些做法可能暂时掩盖支持不足，却延长原本已经需要调整的运行。
另一种风险，是把任何暂时下降都当成应该立即结束的理由。有些工作具有正常的阶段变化，有些责任仍然必须履行，也有些暂时困难能够通过适当支持得到改善。
因此，需要区分短期波动与持续变化，并评估真实责任、恢复可能性及维护成本。
真正有价值的回应，不是强行维持过去的强度，也不是遇到下降就立即退出，而是让投入重新符合现实。

sections.title: 现在可以做什么？
paragraphs: 选择一项你仍然以过去的方式投入时间或资源，但实际支持已经改变的事情。
1. 确认变化： 哪些资源、需求或支持减少了？
2. 检查投入： 目前是否仍然维持原来的强度？
3. 辨认必要部分： 哪些责任或成果必须保留？
4. 调整一种投入： 合理降低频率、缩小范围、重新分工，或安排恢复。
5. 观察结果： 必要部分是否仍然得到保障？持续成本是否变得更可管理？
如果一项活动已经不再需要继续，也可以考虑建立适当的完成与交接安排。

zh-Hans.frozenObservationQuestion: 什么已经不再值得以原来的强度继续维持？
interpretationBoundary: 固定卡义用于观察和反思，不证明你目前的经历、能力或张力，也不预测未来。
这张卡描述的是 ECR 模型中资源、支持或可用容量下降时可能出现的持续成本，并不表示系统已经确认你正在经历健康问题、情绪耗竭、财务损失或其他特定困难。卡片中的「能量」是对可用资源与运行能力的描述，不属于医学测量。是否减少投入、恢复或结束某项事务，应根据实际证据、必要责任与相关风险决定。
sourceProposedQuestion: 什么已经不再值得以原来的强度继续维持？

en.title: DRAIN
en.subtitle: The runtime loses energy or support while continuing to occupy capacity

sections.title: At a Glance
paragraphs: When the resources, support, or practical returns associated with an activity begin to decline, maintaining the same level of investment may not restore earlier results. A useful response is to distinguish what deserves continued support, what needs reduced intensity, and what may require recovery or appropriate closure.

sections.title: What This Card Invites You to Consider
paragraphs: Many arrangements require continuing investment to remain functional. A business needs time, money, and operational support. Family life requires coordination and care. Long-term projects depend on sufficient attention and maintenance resources.

These conditions do not remain unchanged forever. A service may experience declining customer demand, a project may lose previous team support, or a new stage of life may reduce the time once available for certain activities.
Drain invites you to examine whether something is receiving less support than before while continuing to occupy the same or even greater capacity.

Sometimes previous investment makes it difficult to reduce commitment. When results decline, more time is added. When resources become scarce, additional responsibilities are accepted. A project may continue receiving attention even after its practical relevance has diminished.
These responses may prolong an arrangement without necessarily improving its viability.
The useful question is not only how to preserve an existing activity, but whether it still deserves the same level of investment.

Reducing intensity does not automatically mean failure. Some projects can move into maintenance, some responsibilities can be redistributed, and some activities may have achieved their primary purpose and be ready for appropriate closure.
Drain reminds us that when supporting conditions change, the intensity of an activity may need to change as well.

sections.title: How It May Appear in Real Life
paragraphs: Work, Products & Operating Costs
Imagine a company that once offered a popular digital product. Customer demand gradually declines, yet the team continues updating, promoting, and maintaining it at its original intensity.
If revenue and usage continue falling, maintaining the product may consume resources that could support other important services.
Drain suggests examining actual evidence. Is demand genuinely declining? Does the product still involve customer entitlements or contractual obligations? What resources are required to maintain it?
Once essential obligations are protected, some functions might move to lower-intensity maintenance, be integrated into another service, or undergo an appropriate transition toward closure.
The objective is not to discontinue a service whenever demand weakens. It is to keep ongoing investment proportionate to actual value and responsibilities.
Family & Continuing Care
A household may have relied on an established division of domestic and caregiving responsibilities, but changes in work schedules or family circumstances reduce the support previously available.
Expecting one person to maintain every arrangement at its former intensity may make everyday coordination increasingly difficult.

Drain invites the household to review its current support. Which caregiving responsibilities must continue? Which optional activities can become less frequent? Which tasks need redistribution or reliable outside assistance?
Reducing nonessential commitments can preserve resources for important care. But declining support does not justify neglecting children, older relatives, or others who depend on essential assistance.
Appropriate changes should protect continuing responsibilities while making the arrangement more sustainable.
Finances, Assets & Ongoing Expenses
Imagine an asset that previously generated dependable income but has recently produced lower returns while maintenance, financing, or management expenses continue.
Maintaining previous levels of investment based solely on historical performance may create increasing pressure on cash flow.

Drain encourages reassessment using actual income, expenses, and contractual obligations rather than assuming an arrangement should receive the same investment indefinitely because it once performed well.
Possible responses may include improving management, reviewing optional expenses, reconsidering long-term plans, or examining other arrangements with appropriate financial and legal guidance.
This card cannot determine whether an asset should be sold or an investment discontinued. It simply highlights that past value should not replace judgment about present conditions.

sections.title: A Helpful Approach
paragraphs: Align ongoing investment with current resources, responsibilities, and practical value.
Examine three questions:
- Has support changed? Have time, funds, staffing, demand, or other resources declined?
- What still matters? Which obligations, outcomes, or safeguards must continue?
- Is the intensity appropriate? What could operate less frequently, at a smaller scope, through redistribution, or move toward closure?
If an activity remains necessary, a lower-cost and more sustainable maintenance arrangement may be appropriate.
If its original purpose has been fulfilled or the same investment is no longer justified, consider suitable handover or completion conditions.

sections.title: What to Watch For
paragraphs: The main risk associated with Drain is treating declining support as an automatic reason to invest more.
A project performs less well than before, so promotion and development continually increase. An arrangement becomes harder to sustain, yet the same people are expected to contribute more time.
Such responses may temporarily conceal insufficient support while prolonging an activity that needs reconsideration.

The opposite risk is assuming every temporary decline calls for immediate closure. Some activities experience normal fluctuations, some obligations remain essential, and certain difficulties can be improved through appropriate support.
It is therefore important to distinguish short-term variation from sustained change and assess actual responsibilities, recovery possibilities, and maintenance costs.
The useful response is neither forcing previous intensity to continue nor withdrawing whenever support declines. It is bringing investment back into alignment with reality.

sections.title: One Small Action
paragraphs: Choose an activity that still receives your previous level of commitment even though the supporting conditions have changed.
1. Identify the change: Which resources, needs, or forms of support have declined?
2. Review the investment: Is the same intensity still being maintained?
3. Protect essentials: Which responsibilities or outcomes must remain?
4. Adjust one commitment: Reduce frequency, narrow scope, redistribute work, or allow recovery where appropriate.
5. Observe the result: Are essential outcomes protected? Have continuing costs become more manageable?
If an activity no longer needs to continue, consider an appropriate completion or handover process.

en.frozenObservationQuestion: What no longer deserves to be maintained at the same intensity?
interpretationBoundary: Fixed card meanings invite observation and reflection. They do not establish your current experiences, abilities or tensions, or predict the future.

This card describes potential continuing costs within the ECR model when resources, support, or available capacity decline. It does not establish that you are experiencing a medical condition, emotional exhaustion, financial loss, or any other specific difficulty. The term "energy" refers here to practical resources and operating capacity, not a medical measurement. Decisions about reducing intensity, recovery, or closure should be based on evidence, essential obligations, and relevant risks.

zh-Hans.title: 容器
zh-Hans.subtitle: 复杂内容需要一个足够稳定的承载空间

sections.title: 一句话理解
paragraphs: 有些事情不需要更多努力，而是需要一个稳定的环境，让重要的资料、责任或计划能够被妥善安排，不必一直依靠临时处理。

sections.title: 这张卡想提醒什么？
paragraphs: 当生活或工作变得复杂，缺少稳定的安排可能让每件事都需要重新协调。
「容器」提醒你，一个适当的支持环境，可以是清楚的工作流程、可靠的资料管理、固定的家庭安排，或能够专心处理重要事务的空间。
好的容器不需要解决所有问题，而是让不同事情有适当的位置，并允许它们逐步完成。

sections.title: 现实中可能如何出现？
paragraphs: 工作
团队拥有许多重要资料，却没有统一的存放和查找方式。建立清楚的记录与管理权限，可能比不断增加沟通更有效。
家庭
家庭成员经常临时协调孩子的时间。建立适当的日常安排与备用方案，可以减少重复讨论。
个人
如果一项学习计划总被其他事情中断，固定的学习时间和适当的环境，可能比购买更多教材更有帮助。

sections.title: 什么做法更有帮助？
paragraphs: 先建立稳定的支持条件，再增加新的要求。
确认重要事项需要什么空间、资料、时间或管理方式，让它们能够持续进行。

sections.title: 什么情况需要留意？
paragraphs: 容器如果缺少边界，也可能变成无限承接。不是所有新任务都必须加入同一套安排。
稳定的容器应该保护容量，而不是不断扩大负担。

sections.title: 现在可以做什么？
paragraphs: 1. 选择一件经常需要重新协调的事情。
2. 找出它缺少什么稳定条件。
3. 建立一个简单的流程、固定空间或记录方式。
4. 观察是否减少了重复处理。

zh-Hans.frozenObservationQuestion: 什么样的空间会让你更容易把事情放稳，而不是一直应付？
interpretationBoundary: 固定卡义用于观察和反思，不证明你目前的经历、能力或张力，也不预测未来。
这张卡描述的是可能有助于稳定运行的环境条件，不代表系统已确认你的实际生活或工作环境存在问题。
sourceProposedQuestion: 什么样的空间会让你更容易把事情放稳，而不是一直应付？

en.title: CONTAINER
en.subtitle: Complex material needs a stable enough container

sections.title: At a Glance
paragraphs: Sometimes what matters is not greater effort, but a stable environment where information, responsibilities, and plans can be managed without constant intervention.

sections.title: What This Card Invites You to Consider
paragraphs: As life or work becomes more complex, a lack of stable arrangements can make everything require repeated coordination.
Container invites you to consider whether a clearer workflow, reliable information system, consistent household routine, or suitable workspace could provide needed stability.
A good container does not solve every problem immediately. It creates appropriate conditions for important things to be managed and developed.

sections.title: How It May Appear in Real Life
paragraphs: Work
A team has valuable information but no consistent way to store or retrieve it. Clear records and appropriate access controls may help more than additional communication.
Family
Family members repeatedly coordinate children's schedules at the last minute. A workable routine and backup arrangements can reduce unnecessary coordination.
Personal
If learning is repeatedly interrupted, protected study time and a suitable environment may be more useful than purchasing additional resources.

sections.title: A Helpful Approach
paragraphs: Establish reliable supporting conditions before adding new demands.
Identify the space, information, time, or arrangements needed for important activities to continue.

sections.title: What to Watch For
paragraphs: A container without boundaries can become an arrangement expected to hold everything.
A stable container should protect capacity rather than continually absorb new demands.

sections.title: One Small Action
paragraphs: 5. Choose something requiring repeated coordination.
6. Identify the missing supporting condition.
7. Establish a simple process, dedicated space, or record.
8. Observe whether repeated effort decreases.

en.frozenObservationQuestion: What kind of space helps you hold things steadily instead of constantly reacting?
interpretationBoundary: Fixed card meanings invite observation and reflection. They do not establish your current experiences, abilities or tensions, or predict the future.
This card presents possible environmental conditions that support stability. It does not establish that your actual living or working environment has a problem.

frozenCoreMeaning.zh-Hans: 这张牌代表停止、区分、界定与稳定边界的场域条件。
frozenCoreMeaning.en: Field conditions that stop, distinguish, delimit, and stabilize boundaries.

zh-Hans.title: 边界
zh-Hans.subtitle: 清楚的界线让运行知道在哪里停止与稳定

sections.title: 一句话理解
paragraphs: 真正有效的边界，不是把所有事情挡在外面，而是让时间、资源与责任拥有清楚范围，使重要的事情能够稳定进行。

sections.title: 这张卡想提醒什么？
paragraphs: 生活中，许多困难并不是因为我们不愿意合作，而是因为责任与要求的范围不够清楚。
工作中，新任务不断加入，却没有明确优先次序；家庭里，某个人持续承担原本没有约定的责任；个人时间也可能被各种临时要求占据。
「边界」提醒你：适当的支持，有时候并不是接受更多，而是让各方清楚知道什么可以安排、什么需要协商，以及什么已经超出合理范围。
好的边界能减少误解，同时保留必要的合作与变化空间。

sections.title: 现实中可能如何出现？
paragraphs: 工作
一个团队不断收到新的功能要求，导致原定项目反复中断。
明确当前开发范围、必要修复与未来功能的处理方式，可以保护核心交付，同时保留后续改善的机会。
家庭
家庭成员可能习惯由同一个人协调所有事务，却没有明确各自的责任。
通过适当沟通确认分工、时间和备用安排，可以让共同生活更加稳定，而不是把所有协调留给一个人。
个人与财务
一个人可能经常收到借款、协助或其他资源要求，却没有明确自己能够合理提供多少。
清楚说明可用资源和个人责任范围，可以保护必要的财务安排，也避免作出无法持续履行的承诺。

sections.title: 什么做法更有帮助？
paragraphs: 让边界具体、清楚，并与现实责任保持一致。
与其笼统地说「不要再增加事情」，不如明确说明当前能够接受什么、需要怎样的协商，以及哪些事项必须按照已有责任继续处理。
边界也可以随实际条件改变而重新检查，不需要永远维持同一种安排。

sections.title: 什么情况需要留意？
paragraphs: 边界最大的风险，是从必要保护逐渐变成拒绝所有变化。
如果任何新建议、资讯或支持都被排除，原本帮助稳定的规则，也可能阻碍进一步改善。
另一方面，边界不应只停留在口头表达。如果缺乏实际分工、时间安排或执行机制，同样的问题可能持续出现。
有效的边界既能保护重要资源，也允许经过适当判断的新需要进入。

sections.title: 现在可以做什么？
paragraphs: 1. 选择一件责任或要求不够清楚的事情。
2. 确认自己实际需要负责的范围。
3. 向相关人员说明可以接受什么、哪些需要另行协商。
4. 观察沟通与执行是否变得更清楚。

zh-Hans.frozenObservationQuestion: 什么界线一旦说清楚，会让整个环境更容易运作？
interpretationBoundary: 固定卡义用于观察和反思，不证明你目前的经历、能力或张力，也不预测未来。
这张卡描述的是可能有助于稳定运行的边界与环境条件，不代表系统已经确认你的个人关系或工作安排存在边界问题。合理边界仍须尊重实际承诺、法律责任、安全与相关人员的权益。
sourceProposedQuestion: 什么界线一旦说清楚，会让整个环境更容易运作？

en.title: BOUNDARY
en.subtitle: Clear limits show the runtime where to stop and stabilize

sections.title: At a Glance
paragraphs: Effective boundaries do not shut everything out. They establish clear limits for time, resources, and responsibilities so that important activities can function reliably.

sections.title: What This Card Invites You to Consider
paragraphs: Many difficulties arise not from an unwillingness to cooperate, but from unclear limits around responsibilities and expectations.

At work, additional tasks may accumulate without agreed priorities. At home, someone may gradually take on responsibilities that were never clearly discussed. Personal time may also become occupied by constant requests.
Boundary invites you to recognize that support sometimes comes from clearer limits rather than greater availability.
Effective boundaries reduce misunderstandings while preserving room for appropriate cooperation and change.

sections.title: How It May Appear in Real Life
paragraphs: Work
A team receives constant feature requests, repeatedly interrupting planned work.
Defining current scope, essential fixes, and future development procedures can protect delivery while allowing later improvements.
Family
Family members may rely on one person to coordinate nearly everything without clearly defined responsibilities.
Agreeing on roles, schedules, and backup arrangements can make everyday life more reliable without concentrating all coordination on one individual.
Personal Life & Finances
Someone may receive frequent requests for loans, assistance, or other resources without clearly defining what they can reasonably provide.
Communicating available capacity and personal limits can help protect essential financial arrangements and prevent commitments that cannot be sustained.

sections.title: A Helpful Approach
paragraphs: Make boundaries specific, understandable, and consistent with real responsibilities.
Rather than simply saying "no more requests," clarify what can be accepted, what requires discussion, and which obligations must still be fulfilled.
Boundaries can be reviewed as circumstances change. They do not need to remain identical forever.

sections.title: What to Watch For
paragraphs: A risk of boundaries is allowing necessary protection to become resistance to all change.
When every new suggestion, piece of information, or form of support is excluded, rules that once provided stability may begin preventing improvement.
Boundaries also need practical implementation. Without clear responsibilities, schedules, or procedures, the same difficulties may continue.
Effective boundaries protect important resources while allowing appropriate new needs to be considered.

sections.title: One Small Action
paragraphs: 5. Choose a situation with unclear expectations or responsibilities.
6. Identify the scope you are genuinely responsible for.
7. Communicate what is manageable and what requires further agreement.
8. Observe whether coordination and execution become clearer.

en.frozenObservationQuestion: Which boundary, if made clear, would make the whole environment easier to operate in?
interpretationBoundary: Fixed card meanings invite observation and reflection. They do not establish your current experiences, abilities or tensions, or predict the future.

This card presents boundary conditions that may support stability. It does not establish that your relationships or work arrangements have boundary problems. Appropriate limits must remain consistent with actual commitments, legal obligations, safety, and the rights of those involved.

zh-Hans.title: 协作
zh-Hans.subtitle: 不同位置通过分工与互补形成更好的承载

sections.title: 一句话理解
paragraphs: 好的协作，不是增加更多参与者，而是让不同的人发挥适当的作用，通过明确分工与互相配合，使重要事务能够更稳定地完成。

sections.title: 这张卡想提醒什么？
paragraphs: 生活中，有些困难并不是因为人手不足，而是现有的能力与责任没有被合理安排。
一个团队可能拥有足够的专业人员，却因为分工不清而重复工作；家庭成员可能都愿意帮忙，却不知道谁负责什么；一项计划也可能长期依靠同一个人完成所有协调。
「协作」提醒你：真正的支持，有时候来自更清楚的角色与互补，而不是要求每个人付出更多。
好的协作允许不同的人拥有不同的能力和责任，同时建立清楚的交接与沟通方式。
真正需要改善的，不一定是参与人数，而是如何让已有资源在适当的位置发挥作用。

sections.title: 现实中可能如何出现？
paragraphs: 工作
生产、财务和管理部门可能各自拥有完整资料，却因为责任与交接方式不清楚，需要不断重复核对。
明确哪个部门负责输入、谁负责验证，以及结果交给谁使用，可以改善协作，而不必让所有人同时处理相同工作。
家庭
家庭可能长期由一人负责孩子安排、家务和重要文件，其他成员则偶尔协助。
更有效的协作，可以是根据实际时间与能力明确分工，让不同成员承担适合的责任，并建立必要的备用安排。
个人与专业合作
一个人可能擅长设计和整理内容，却缺少某些技术或专业能力。
与适当的合作伙伴分工，可能比尝试独自掌握所有技能更有效。涉及专业资格或客户资料的工作，还必须确认合法权限与保密要求。

sections.title: 什么做法更有帮助？
paragraphs: 让责任、能力与资源处于适当的位置。
先确认谁适合负责什么，以及不同工作之间需要怎样交接。
协作不要求每个人承担相同份量，但应让相关人员理解自己的职责，并有机会讨论是否能够合理履行。

sections.title: 什么情况需要留意？
paragraphs: 协作最大的风险，是参与者增加了，责任却没有更清楚。
当每个人都认为别人会处理，重要事项可能被遗漏；当所有决定仍然集中在一个人身上，所谓的共同承担也可能只是增加协调工作。
合作如果没有清楚的角色边界，共同承担可能变成共同混乱。

sections.title: 现在可以做什么？
paragraphs: 1. 选择一项需要多人参与的事务。
2. 列出目前由谁负责哪些部分。
3. 找出重复、遗漏或责任过度集中的环节。
4. 与相关人员讨论一项更合适的分工或交接。
5. 观察工作是否更顺畅、负担是否更合理。

zh-Hans.frozenObservationQuestion: 哪一部分如果交给更合适的位置，你会立刻轻很多？
interpretationBoundary: 固定卡义用于观察和反思，不证明你目前的经历、能力或张力，也不预测未来。
这张卡描述的是通过角色互补、协调与共享责任形成支持的环境条件，并不代表系统已经确认你擅长团队合作，或某个人应该替你承担责任。实际协作仍需尊重参与者的意愿、能力、权限及合理边界。
sourceProposedQuestion: 哪一部分如果交给更合适的位置，你会立刻轻很多？

en.title: COLLABORATION
en.subtitle: Different positions create better capacity through complementarity

sections.title: At a Glance
paragraphs: Effective collaboration is not simply about involving more people. It brings together complementary capabilities and clear responsibilities so that important work can be completed more reliably.

sections.title: What This Card Invites You to Consider
paragraphs: Some difficulties arise not from too few people, but from unclear responsibilities and poorly arranged capabilities.

A team may have sufficient expertise yet duplicate work because roles overlap. Family members may be willing to help without knowing who is responsible for what. A project may depend excessively on one person for coordination.
Collaboration reminds you that meaningful support often comes from clearer roles and complementary contributions rather than asking everyone to do more.
Effective collaboration allows people to contribute differently while maintaining clear communication and handovers.
The solution may lie less in increasing participation and more in arranging existing resources appropriately.

sections.title: How It May Appear in Real Life
paragraphs: Work
Production, finance, and management may each possess useful information, yet unclear responsibilities create repeated reconciliation.
Defining who records information, who verifies it, and who uses the results can improve collaboration without making everyone perform identical tasks.
Family
A household may rely on one person for childcare schedules, domestic tasks, and important documents while others help occasionally.
Better collaboration may involve assigning responsibilities according to available time and capabilities, with appropriate backup arrangements.
Personal & Professional Cooperation
Someone may be capable in design and content organization but lack particular technical or professional skills.

Working with an appropriately qualified collaborator may be more effective than attempting to master everything alone. Professional authorization and confidentiality requirements must still be respected.

sections.title: A Helpful Approach
paragraphs: Place responsibilities, capabilities, and resources where they fit best.
Clarify who is suited to each responsibility and how the different contributions should connect.
Collaboration does not require identical workloads, but participants should understand their roles and be able to discuss whether those responsibilities are manageable.

sections.title: What to Watch For
paragraphs: The main risk of collaboration is increasing participation without clarifying ownership.
When everyone assumes someone else will act, important tasks may be missed. When every decision still depends on one person, shared work may simply create additional coordination.
Without clear roles and boundaries, shared responsibility can become shared confusion.

sections.title: One Small Action
paragraphs: 6. Choose an activity involving several people.
7. Identify who currently handles each responsibility.
8. Find duplication, missing ownership, or excessive dependence on one person.
9. Discuss one more appropriate division or handover.
10. Observe whether coordination improves and responsibilities become more manageable.

en.frozenObservationQuestion: What would become lighter if it moved to a more appropriate role or position?
interpretationBoundary: Fixed card meanings invite observation and reflection. They do not establish your current experiences, abilities or tensions, or predict the future.

This card presents environmental conditions that support collaboration through complementary roles and shared responsibilities. It does not establish that you possess exceptional teamwork skills or that another person should assume your obligations. Actual collaboration requires respect for participants' willingness, capabilities, authority, and appropriate boundaries.

frozenCoreMeaning.zh-Hans: 这张牌代表通过交换、回应与相互运动形成变化的条件。
frozenCoreMeaning.en: Conditions in which change proceeds through exchange, response, and reciprocal movement.

zh-Hans.title: 交换
zh-Hans.subtitle: 资源、回应与价值需要保持双向流动

sections.title: 一句话理解
paragraphs: 真正有效的交换，不只是持续付出，而是让投入与回应之间建立合理联系，使双方能够获得有意义的价值，并支持关系或合作持续发展。

sections.title: 这张卡想提醒什么？
paragraphs: 生活中，许多事情需要通过交换才能持续。工作需要付出与反馈，合作需要资源与责任之间的协调，家庭关系也需要适当的沟通、理解与支持。
「交换」邀请你观察：目前的投入是否获得了能够帮助事情继续发展的回应？
例如，一项服务不断增加功能，却很少了解顾客是否真正需要；一个人长期协助别人，却没有机会讨论自己的资源限制；一个团队持续提交资料，却从未收到能够改善工作的反馈。
有效交换不意味着每个人必须付出相同时间、金钱或劳动。不同角色可能具有不同责任，而有意义的回应也不一定是物质回报。
真正重要的是，投入与回应之间存在清楚、适当且可以持续的联系。

sections.title: 现实中可能如何出现？
paragraphs: 工作与顾客服务
团队持续开发产品，但很少收集实际顾客反馈。
建立适当的反馈渠道，可以帮助团队了解哪些成果真正有价值，避免不断投入到顾客不需要的功能。
家庭与关系
家庭成员可能长期由一人承担大部分协调，其他成员却不了解实际工作量。
通过沟通需要、明确分工和提供适当支持，可以改善长期单向投入的问题。
这不代表照顾必须以等量回报交换，尤其孩子或需要照顾的人不应被要求承担不适当的责任。
财务与专业合作
一项专业服务可能持续投入时间与资源，却没有明确服务范围、收费或交付标准。
清楚约定双方责任、合理报酬与交付内容，可以减少误解，让合作更容易持续。

sections.title: 什么做法更有帮助？
paragraphs: 检查投入与回应之间，是否具有真正有效的联系。
先确认自己或相关人员正在提供什么，再了解对方实际需要什么，以及双方如何知道交换已经产生价值。
如果长期缺乏回应，可以考虑改善沟通、明确约定、调整投入范围，或重新评估合作方式。

sections.title: 什么情况需要留意？
paragraphs: 交换最大的风险，是长期只有单方面投入，却缺少足以支持持续运行的回应。
另一种风险，是把所有关系都当成必须计算回报的交易。某些关系具有不对等的照顾责任，不能只用付出和获得的数量来判断。
良好的交换重视持续性与合理回应，而不是要求每个人付出完全相同。

sections.title: 现在可以做什么？
paragraphs: 1. 选择一项需要长期投入的合作或安排。
2. 写下双方分别投入什么、需要什么。
3. 找出目前缺少的反馈、沟通或资源流动。
4. 尝试改善一个交换环节。
5. 观察双方是否更容易持续参与。

zh-Hans.frozenObservationQuestion: 哪里需要的不是更多投入，而是更好的交换方式？
interpretationBoundary: 固定卡义用于观察和反思，不证明你目前的经历、能力或张力，也不预测未来。
这张卡描述的是通过资源交换、回应与相互流动形成支持的环境条件，不代表系统已确认你正处于不公平关系、付出过多或回报不足的情况。实际交换仍须尊重自愿参与、现有责任、合理边界及相关权益。
sourceProposedQuestion: 哪里需要的不是更多投入，而是更好的交换方式？

en.title: EXCHANGE
en.subtitle: Resources, response, and value need reciprocal movement

sections.title: At a Glance
paragraphs: Meaningful exchange is not simply about giving more. It creates a workable relationship between contribution and response, allowing value to move in ways that support continued cooperation.

sections.title: What This Card Invites You to Consider
paragraphs: Many activities depend on exchange to continue. Work involves effort and feedback, cooperation requires coordinated resources and responsibilities, and family life benefits from communication, understanding, and appropriate support.
Exchange invites you to examine whether contributions receive responses that help the arrangement continue effectively.

A service may keep adding features without learning whether customers need them. Someone may provide ongoing assistance without discussing their own resource limits. A team may submit information repeatedly without receiving feedback that improves its work.

Meaningful exchange does not require everyone to contribute identical amounts of time, money, or labor. Different roles involve different responsibilities, and a useful response is not necessarily financial.
What matters is a clear, appropriate, and sustainable connection between contribution and response.

sections.title: How It May Appear in Real Life
paragraphs: Work & Customer Service
A team continues developing a product but rarely receives meaningful customer feedback.
An appropriate feedback channel can reveal which improvements create value and reduce investment in features that customers do not need.
Family & Relationships
One household member may handle most coordination while others remain unaware of the workload.
Discussing needs, clarifying responsibilities, and offering appropriate support can improve the arrangement.
Caregiving does not require equal repayment, particularly from children or people who depend on care.
Finances & Professional Cooperation
A professional service may require continuing time and resources without clearly defined scope, fees, or deliverables.
Clear agreements about responsibilities, appropriate compensation, and expected outcomes can reduce misunderstandings and support sustainable cooperation.

sections.title: A Helpful Approach
paragraphs: Examine whether contributions and responses are meaningfully connected.
Clarify what is being contributed, what the other party actually needs, and how both can recognize whether the exchange is useful.
Where responses remain insufficient, consider clearer communication, agreements, revised commitments, or a different cooperative arrangement.

sections.title: What to Watch For
paragraphs: The main risk is ongoing one-way contribution without sufficient response to sustain the arrangement.

Another risk is treating every relationship as a transaction requiring measurable repayment. Some relationships involve unequal caregiving obligations that cannot be evaluated through identical contributions.
Healthy exchange values sustainability and appropriate responses rather than exact equality in what everyone gives.

sections.title: One Small Action
paragraphs: 6. Choose an arrangement requiring ongoing contributions.
7. Identify what each party contributes and needs.
8. Find a missing feedback or resource exchange.
9. Improve one part of the exchange.
10. Observe whether participation becomes more sustainable.

en.frozenObservationQuestion: Where is the need not more effort, but a better exchange?
interpretationBoundary: Fixed card meanings invite observation and reflection. They do not establish your current experiences, abilities or tensions, or predict the future.

This card presents environmental conditions involving reciprocal contribution, feedback, and value. It does not establish that you are in an unfair relationship or contributing more than you receive. Actual exchanges must respect voluntary participation, existing responsibilities, appropriate boundaries, and the rights of those involved.
sourceProposedQuestion: Where is the need not more effort, but a better exchange?

frozenCoreMeaning.zh-Hans: 这张牌代表通过流动、循环与绕开阻力来支持变化的环境节律。
frozenCoreMeaning.en: A field rhythm that supports change through movement, circulation, and adaptation around obstacles.

zh-Hans.title: 节律
zh-Hans.subtitle: 可持续速度比持续加速更重要

sections.title: 一句话理解
paragraphs: 真正稳定的节奏，不是每一天都保持高效率，而是能够根据现实需要调整速度，让行动、停顿与恢复相互配合，使重要的事情持续前进。

sections.title: 这张卡想提醒什么？
paragraphs: 生活中，我们很容易把忙碌当成进展。工作不断增加，就尝试加快速度；计划暂时停顿，就担心自己落后；即使一项重要任务已经完成，也可能立即安排下一项工作。
然而，持续运作需要的不只是行动，也包括整理、检查和恢复的空间。
「节律」邀请你观察：目前的生活或工作安排，是否存在适当的行动与停顿？还是所有时间都被要求保持同样的强度？
好的节奏并不是永远缓慢。有些阶段确实需要集中执行，有些阶段则适合检查成果、调整方向或减少投入。
真正有价值的节律，是让速度能够随着现实条件改变，而不是要求自己永远加速。

sections.title: 现实中可能如何出现？
paragraphs: 工作与项目
团队持续开发新功能，却没有安排足够时间进行测试、修复和验收。
建立适当的开发、验证与交付节奏，可以让工作持续形成可靠成果，而不是不断累积未完成事项。
家庭与日常生活
家庭的工作、学校与活动安排可能十分紧密，缺少适当的缓冲时间。
保留必要的休息与转换空间，并根据实际情况调整活动频率，可以减少持续赶时间的负担。
学习与财务管理
学习新技能时，持续增加课程未必比安排学习、练习和复查更有效。
财务管理也可以建立定期检查收支与责任的节奏，而不必因为每一次市场变化，就立即重新决定长期计划。

sections.title: 什么做法更有帮助？
paragraphs: 让行动强度与实际资源保持一致。
可以将安排分成三个部分：
- 行动： 集中处理当前重要事务。
- 检查： 确认成果、反馈与下一步。
- 恢复： 保留适当时间和资源，支持持续运行。
不必为所有活动设置相同节奏。重要的是让工作强度、实际责任与可用容量相互配合。

sections.title: 什么情况需要留意？
paragraphs: 节律最大的风险，是将持续忙碌误认为持续进展。
如果每一天都安排得没有余地，原本可以用于检查、改善与恢复的时间可能逐渐消失。
另一方面，节律也不能成为无限延迟必要行动的理由。涉及安全、明确期限或必须履行的责任时，仍然需要及时处理。
好的节奏不是固定地快或慢，而是在适当的时候采取适当的速度。

sections.title: 现在可以做什么？
paragraphs: 1. 选择一项最近持续占用你时间的工作或安排。
2. 观察目前是否只有不断执行，却缺少检查和恢复。
3. 为下一阶段安排适当的执行、检查与停顿时间。
4. 观察成果是否更稳定，是否减少不必要的赶工。

zh-Hans.frozenObservationQuestion: 你的现实现在需要加速，还是需要重新找回节奏？
interpretationBoundary: 固定卡义用于观察和反思，不证明你目前的经历、能力或张力，也不预测未来。
这张卡描述的是可能支持持续运行的环境节律，并不代表系统已经确认你目前工作过度、需要减速，或存在健康问题。适当节奏应根据真实责任、资源、期限和个人情况决定。
sourceProposedQuestion: 你的现实现在需要加速，还是需要重新找回节奏？

en.title: RHYTHM
en.subtitle: A sustainable pace matters more than continuous acceleration

sections.title: At a Glance
paragraphs: A sustainable rhythm does not require maximum productivity every day. It allows action, pauses, and recovery to work together so meaningful progress can continue over time.

sections.title: What This Card Invites You to Consider
paragraphs: We often confuse constant activity with progress. As workloads increase, we try to move faster. When plans pause, we worry about falling behind. Even after completing an important task, we may immediately begin another.
Yet sustainable operation requires more than action. It also needs time for review, adjustment, and recovery.
Rhythm invites you to consider whether your current arrangements allow appropriate periods of movement and pause, or whether everything is expected to continue at the same intensity.
A good rhythm is not necessarily slow. Some stages require concentrated effort, while others benefit from evaluating results or reducing intensity.
Meaningful rhythm allows pace to respond to reality rather than demanding continuous acceleration.

sections.title: How It May Appear in Real Life
paragraphs: Work & Projects
A team continually develops new features without allocating sufficient time for testing, correction, and acceptance.
A workable development, verification, and delivery rhythm can produce reliable results rather than an expanding collection of unfinished tasks.
Family & Everyday Life
Household schedules may become tightly packed with work, school, and other activities.
Allowing time for rest and transitions, while adjusting optional commitments, can reduce the pressure of constantly rushing.
Learning & Financial Management
When developing a new skill, continually adding courses may be less useful than combining learning, practice, and review.
Financial management can also benefit from periodic checks of income, spending, and obligations rather than repeatedly revising long-term plans in response to every market movement.

sections.title: A Helpful Approach
paragraphs: Align the intensity of activity with available resources.
Create room for three elements:
- Action: Focused work on current priorities.
- Review: Checking outcomes, feedback, and next steps.
- Recovery: Preserving sufficient time and resources for continuity.
Different activities may require different rhythms. The aim is to keep demands, responsibilities, and capacity appropriately aligned.

sections.title: What to Watch For
paragraphs: The main risk is mistaking constant busyness for meaningful progress.
When every day is filled completely, time needed for review, improvement, and recovery may disappear.
Rhythm should also not become an excuse for indefinitely delaying essential action. Safety concerns, firm deadlines, and valid obligations may still require prompt attention.
A good rhythm is neither permanently fast nor permanently slow. It matches the pace to the situation.

sections.title: One Small Action
paragraphs: 5. Choose an activity that has required sustained attention.
6. Check whether it involves continuous execution without sufficient review or recovery.
7. Arrange a more suitable balance of action, review, and pauses.
8. Observe whether outcomes become more reliable and unnecessary rushing decreases.

en.frozenObservationQuestion: Does your reality need more speed, or a better rhythm?
interpretationBoundary: Fixed card meanings invite observation and reflection. They do not establish your current experiences, abilities or tensions, or predict the future.

This card presents environmental rhythms that may support sustainable activity. It does not establish that you are overworking, need to slow down, or have a health condition. An appropriate pace depends on actual responsibilities, resources, deadlines, and individual circumstances.
sourceProposedQuestion: Does your reality need more speed, or a better rhythm?
